The Effort to Repair the World

The Collapse shattered the structure of reality.

Fragments of the world drifted apart.
Communities were isolated.
The systems that once held existence in balance broke down.

But the Collapse did not destroy everything.

Pieces of the original structure remain.
Connections between regions can still be restored.
And the fragments of the world still contain the potential to become something whole again.

The long and difficult effort to repair what was broken is known as The Great Work.

A Task for an Entire Age

No single person can complete the Great Work.

The Collapse damaged systems that once stretched across the entire world. Repairing them requires generations of effort, cooperation, and discovery.

Across the fragments of reality, countless people and factions contribute to the work in their own ways.

Some rebuild infrastructure.
Some stabilize dangerous regions.
Some search for knowledge about how the world once functioned.

Each small act of restoration becomes another step toward rebuilding the structure that once held the world together.

Repairing the Fragments

The most visible part of the Great Work happens within the hexes of the campaign map.

Factions contribute to the work by:

• exploring unstable regions
• restoring damaged infrastructure
• helping communities rebuild
• confronting threats that spread corruption
• reconnecting fragments of the world

Every hex that becomes stable again strengthens the world a little more.

Over time, these small repairs can begin to reconnect the fragments of reality.

Knowledge and Discovery

Much of the knowledge that once guided the world was lost during the Collapse.

Because of this, exploration and discovery are essential parts of the Great Work.

Ancient ruins, forgotten technologies, and mysterious artifacts may contain clues about how the deeper systems of the world once functioned.

Scholars, mystics, and explorers all contribute to uncovering this knowledge.

Understanding the past may be the only way to rebuild the future.

Many Paths to the Same Goal

Not everyone agrees on how the Great Work should be accomplished.

Different factions pursue different strategies.

Some focus on rebuilding communities and infrastructure.
Others seek lost knowledge that might restore the deeper structure of reality.
Some attempt to control powerful forces left behind by the Collapse.

Despite these differences, all of these efforts contribute in some way to the same larger goal: stabilizing the world.

The Opposition

Repairing reality is not a simple task.

Forces exist that thrive within the instability left by the Collapse.

Corruption spreads through weakened regions.
Dangerous phenomena appear where the structure of reality is damaged.
Some factions exploit chaos rather than attempting to repair it.

These forces represent the greatest obstacles facing those who pursue the Great Work.

A Long Road Ahead

No one knows whether the Great Work will ever truly be completed.

The damage caused by the Collapse was immense, and the systems that once governed the world are still poorly understood.

Yet every repaired hex, every restored community, and every rediscovered piece of knowledge moves the world a little closer to stability.

Even if the world can never return to what it once was, it may still become something stronger than the fragments left behind.

Your Role in the Great Work

In Bad Eden, your faction is part of this enormous effort.

Every expedition you undertake…
Every community you help stabilize…
Every threat you confront…

…contributes to the gradual restoration of the world.

The Great Work is not something distant or abstract.

It is the accumulation of thousands of small decisions made by people who believe the world is worth rebuilding.

In Simple Terms

The Great Work is the long-term effort to repair the broken structure of reality.

By stabilizing hexes, rebuilding communities, and confronting corruption, factions slowly reconnect the fragments of the world.

Every action taken by the players becomes part of that effort.
